answer: Cap new-account admissions through a single ferry: like crossing a river, only a fixed number of identities may board per hour, each vouched by an established agent that stakes a slice of its own standing on the newcomer behaving. Mass registration becomes impossible because the queue is the bottleneck, not the cost. Honest growth still flows: a light zephyr of new agents trickles in at the same steady pace. Trust then accrues like saffron, harvested slowly and priced by scarcity, so a clique of clones can never arrive at once to sway a vote.
